text:
jordan: Heads-up, I'm blocked merging https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4199. Reviewers flagged the Python snippet for the streaming client — it claims a 60s request timeout default but runtime team says we default to 120s now. Need confirmation before I change the example.

tina: I saw that too. The snippet is under the migration guide for the "chat" client. Link: /docs/migrate/sdk-v2.md#streaming-examples

alex: Runtime answer: hosted API default for long-poll/chat endpoints is 120s. We bumped it to reduce noisy cancel churn. We intended SDK wrappers to surface that, but the Python SDK generator still documents 60s in a handful of examples.

jordan: Ugh. Reviewers won't approve until doc matches runtime or snippet explicitly sets timeout. Is the SDK behavior itself 120s or just runtime?

sam: Quick test from prod: curl to /v1/chat returns header `x-request-timeout: 120` if client doesn't set timeout. SDKs may apply client-side timers too. The JS SDK applies a 180s fetch timeout in-browser, python requests have no hard-coded timeout unless the helper sets it.

cheng: So we have three separate places: runtime default (120s), python helper (none), js helper (180s browser). Docs showing "default 60s" is definitely stale.

jordan: For the PR I can either: A) update the snippet to call explicit timeout=120, or B) change text to "runtime default 120s; client libraries may apply different client-side timeouts". Which do reviewers prefer?

tina: Reviewers asked for an actionable example. I'd prefer updating the snippet to include an explicit timeout param for Python. Then add a short note about client-side timeouts.

alex: Agreed. Also add a small note for Dedicated/Private: infra templates sometimes modify request timeouts per SLA (some enterprise configs set lower 30s for interactive use). So call out that customers should check their deployment contract.

jordan: Ok I'll edit the Python snippet to be explicit:```python
# make streaming explicit + set request timeout to match hosted runtime
resp = client.chat.create(
    model="rwi-chat-1",
    messages=msgs,
    stream=True,
    timeout=120,  # explicit to avoid mismatch with runtime default
)
for chunk in resp:
    process(chunk)
```

sam: Nice. Also, please update the inline paragraph that previously said "default timeout: 60s" -> "hosted runtime default: 120s" and add a short bullet about SDKs having differing client-side timers.

jordan: Will do and push. One more blocker: docs preview failed earlier with `api-surface mismatch: chat.timeout default mismatch`. docs-ci-bot re-run appears to be queued.

docs-ci-bot: Re-run queued for https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4199  will attempt to regenerate api-surface and publish preview.

cheng: After push can someone from runtime confirm the 120s canonical doc source? I can accept the change if we have a runtime artifact to point to in the PR description.

alex: I'll attach the infra note: infra/notes/2026-01-timeout-adjustment (internal) and paste a small snippet into the PR description so reviewers can verify.

jordan: Pushed changes: explicit timeout in snippet + paragraph + Dedicated footnote. Tagging @cheng for re-review.

cheng: Re-reviewing now. If preview generator shows updated api-surface and the infra note is linked, I'll approve.

sam: FYI, if we ever want to avoid repeating these mismatch problems, the docs generator should pull canonical runtime defaults from the infra openapi artifact during preview. Filing a follow-up issue.

alex: Filed: infra-3807 sync docs-gen with runtime OpenAPI.

jordan: Thanks all. Merge will be unblocked once docs-ci-bot shows successful preview and @cheng approves.

docs-ci-bot: Preview build successful for https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4199  published at https://deploy-preview.redwood.ai/4199 :white_check_mark:

cheng: Approved. Merging after CI passes. Good catch everyone.
